# Firstwater

> Facilitated group sound sessions in Denver, what many people search for as a sound bath or sound meditation: seventy-five minutes of engineered sub-bass and live instruments with a formal opening and close, built by a professional music producer. Each night is built around something worth putting down.

## Pages

- [Firstwater](https://thefirstwater.co/): Sound sessions in Denver, led by Daniel (also known as Firstwater), opened and closed with ceremony.
- [Sessions](https://thefirstwater.co/sessions/): Every night Firstwater runs, each built around something worth putting down.
- [Healing from Breakups](https://thefirstwater.co/sessions/healing-from-breakups/): A sound session in Denver for anyone carrying the end of a relationship.
- [Grief](https://thefirstwater.co/sessions/grief/): A sound session in Denver for people carrying a death, held at the quiet end.
- [Sunday Downshift](https://thefirstwater.co/sessions/sunday-downshift/): A recurring Sunday evening sound session in Denver for closing the week.
- [New to Denver](https://thefirstwater.co/sessions/new-to-denver/): A sound session for people who just moved to Denver, with time to meet others after.
- [Couples Reconnection](https://thefirstwater.co/sessions/couples/): A date-night sound session in Denver for two people, side by side.
- [Laid Off](https://thefirstwater.co/sessions/laid-off/): A sound session for people leaving a company and the teams they leave behind.
- [Quiet New Year's](https://thefirstwater.co/sessions/quiet-new-years/): An alternative to the New Year's party in Denver, for entering the year rested.
- [Singles](https://thefirstwater.co/sessions/singles/): A social night in Denver with sound at the center, for meeting someone in a calm space.
- [Sleep Descent](https://thefirstwater.co/sessions/sleep/): A recorded sound descent for the end of the day, free for the email list first.
- [Corporate & Group Sessions](https://thefirstwater.co/corporate/): Facilitated sound sessions for teams, offsites, and retreats in Denver, from $450.
- [FAQ](https://thefirstwater.co/faq/): What a sound session is, what happens at a session, and what to bring.
- [About](https://thefirstwater.co/about/): Daniel, also known as Firstwater, a professional music producer holding sound sessions in Denver.
- [Contact](https://thefirstwater.co/contact/): Reach Firstwater about sessions, teams, venues, or press.

## Blog

- [Should I bring someone?](https://thefirstwater.co/blog/should-i-bring-someone.html): First-person piece from the Firstwater facilitator answering whether to attend a sound session alone or with a friend or partner. Covers what the seventy-five minutes is like either way (lying down under blankets in low light, no talking, no sharing), what a companion changes about the arrival and the tea afterward, the optional invitation offered on some nights, and the separate couples session built for two people side by side.
- [What people ask me about crying](https://thefirstwater.co/blog/what-if-i-cry.html): First-person essay from the Firstwater facilitator on crying during a sound bath. Covers how common it is, what actually happens in the space when someone cries (nobody turns, the hour continues), why people arrive having already decided it would be a failure of composure, and the door policy. Written for anyone deciding whether to come to a session about grief, a breakup, or a job loss.
- [A nap is a legitimate outcome](https://thefirstwater.co/blog/a-nap-is-a-legitimate-outcome.html): First-person essay from the Firstwater facilitator on falling asleep during a sound bath. Explains what the hour is offered as, the time, the space, and a practice, and describes the range of honest outcomes: a window for some people, an hour of real sleep for others, something further for a few. Written for anyone who went under and wondered whether they did it wrong.
- [Isolated together](https://thefirstwater.co/blog/isolated-together.html): First-person essay from the Firstwater facilitator: most sound baths are private experiences lined up on yoga mats. What a group adds over headphones at home, and why the sessions are built to be together.
- [I'm not a skeptic, and I'm not a believer](https://thefirstwater.co/blog/does-sound-healing-work.html): First-person essay from the Firstwater facilitator, a music producer, on whether sound healing works. Rejects the cellular and cancer-cure claims as false, explains the real oncotripsy research they are a cartoon of (ultrasound near 500 kHz, about eleven octaves above a singing bowl), and argues the value is regulated attention and community, not the sound's chemistry. Covers the underwhelm case and how to tell honest facilitation from snake oil.
